findings.text: 9 chemotype(s); the largest holds 7 of 20 molecules -- a series of several scaffolds has no common frame, and an alignment will invent one
the common framework (framework of the largest chemotype) has 17 heavy atoms, about 94% of a typical molecule, and 40% of the set can be cut at it
the 17 shared framework atoms sit 2.4 A apart between molecules, over the best of their matches (8 of 20 carry them) -- the molecules are not in a common frame

the file has 11 numeric column(s) of its own (mw, n_papers, depth, mwila_hcl_adj, mwila_h2so4_raw, mwila_h2so4_adj, mwila_pooled_raw, mwila_pooled_adj and 3 more); with them the descriptor baseline is +0.281 in q2 against the computed descriptors (95% interval +0.172 to +0.552); the activity under another name, by a correlation above 0.95: mwila_hcl_adj, mwila_pooled_raw -- these columns predict the activity, so they are measurements or forms of the activity and not descriptions of the structure. They are not used. If some of them are real descriptors, such as the conditions of the measurement, name them (descriptors=..., or --descriptors on the command line) and run again
the aligned model is -0.059 in q2 against counts (95% interval -0.380 to +0.183) -- the frame gains nothing over counts
the aligned model is -0.447 in q2 against invariant (95% interval -0.883 to -0.029) -- the frame gains nothing over invariant
the aligned model is -0.783 in q2 against descriptors (95% interval -1.165 to -0.594) -- descriptors alone do as well, so the geometry adds nothing on this set

why: descriptors alone match the 3D model, so a field model here is an expensive way to count atoms; use the fields only if the co-field is the purpose
